full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case briefly are that the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 324/1982 in the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka as plaintiff against one Mohammad Hossain : and others for specific performance of contract on the basis of a written agreement for sale dated 7.4.1981. The said suit was decreed expanse by judgment and order dated 29.6.1983. The suit having been decreed the petitioner was allowed to take back his document from the Court. The petitioner as decree holder put the decree passed in the aforesaid suit in execution on 28M.1983 in Title Execution Case No. 49 of 1983 of the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The executing Court executed and registered a deed of conveyance in favour of the petitioner on 6.12.S3 in the office of the District Registrar, Dhaka in terms of the decree. Tne petitioner them filed an application on 3.4 1984 for issuance of writ of delivery of possession of the decretal property. While the matter was thus pending, an application dated 6.6 84 was addressed to the Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka by one Jamaluddin Ahmed, Sub-Inspector of Police, C.I.D. Bangladesh O.P.No 1 Dhaka. It was stated in the said application that the said Sub-Inspector was asked by the police Head Quarters to inquire into the forged Bainanama submitted by the petitioner as Opposite party No.4. Jane Alain had submitted a prayer that the said Bainanama was a forged one and the decree in the aforesaid suit was passed on the basil of the Said foiled Bainanama. The Sub-Inspector prayed for permission to conduct an inquiry in the matter and to take the Bainataama in custody for comparison and opinion. The Subordinate Judge upon a perusal of the said application observed in. his order dated 9 6 84 that necessary permission was required to be obtained from District Judge. His order dated 20.6.84 shows that another application was filed by the Sub-Inspector to the District Judge which was forwarded to him with an order of the District Judge for according permission. Accordingly, permission was accorded for seizure of the document in question. On the following day i.e.21.6.84 the Subordinate Judge passed Order for retiling the Sainanarna and further observed that the Police Officer concerned may seize the document direct from the plaintiff (Petitioner) or he might wait till the document was reeled in Court. 

 4. We find considerable substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner The learned Advocates appearing for the State and Opposite-party No. 4 have not disputed the proposition of law sought to be advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The learned Advocate for the Opposite party No.4 has only prayed that the petitioner should not be allowed to take back the disputed document from the Court so that the Subordinate judge can hold an inquiry as required under section 476 Cr. P.C. when the disputed document has been given in evidence in the aforesaid Civil Suit. The law provides that cognizance of an offence- of alleged forgery in respect of that document can be taken only on the basis of a complaint filed by the Court in which the document has been produced and used. The Opposite party No.4 instead of approaching the police ought to have approached the Subordinate Judge for holding inquiry under section 476 Cr.P.C. It is on record that the O.P.No.4 and others in the meantime filed T.S 225/84 challenging the decree passed in T.S.324/82. Obviously in the facts of the instant case the inquiry by the police would be abortive for, the police cannot usefully submit charge-sheet in the case nor the law permits an inquiry by the police when the document has been produced before a court in connection with a proceeding in the said court. Although it is true to say that a proceeding for quashment is considered .premature at the stage of injury or investigation, but in the facts of the present case we think that the according of permission by the District judge to the Police amounts to an abuse of the process of the Court. The law requires the Court itself to hold an inquiry, if necessary, in a matter like this and the Court cannot divest itself of its jurisdiction to hold such inquiry and allow another agency to conduct the same. This, in our opinion, being the position in law, we think that both the District Judge and the Subordinate Judge acted illegally in permitting the C.I.D. Sub-Inspector to seize the disputed document and to hold inquiry as prayed for.
